This notebook records the steps taken to develop a reproducible platform container for this project.

We're next going to deal with developer tools. These are not intended to be
part of the scientific substrate, but are necessary for development of the
project. They pretty much encapsulate the way I like to code.

There are 3 developer tools I don't go anywhere without:

- `arf` — the R console of the future
- `rv` and `uv` for project package management
- `code` — Sorry, I'm not yet sold on `nvim`!

We'll use the custom `Installable` dataclass for this step. 
So, for example, our favourite R console, `arf`, can be represented like so:

```{python}
arf_pkg = Installable(
    name="arf",
    kind="cargo",
    path="/root/.cargo/bin/arf",
    commands=[
        "curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf https://github.com/eitsupi/arf/releases/latest/download/arf-console-installer.sh | sh",
        """
        ARF_BIN="$(find /root/.cargo/bin /home -path '*/.cargo/bin/arf' -type f 2>/dev/null | head -n 1)"
        if [ -z "$ARF_BIN" ]; then
            ARF_BIN="$(find / -path '*/.cargo/bin/arf' -type f 2>/dev/null | head -n 1)"
        fi

        test -n "$ARF_BIN"
        install -m 0755 "$ARF_BIN" /usr/local/bin/arf
        """
    ]
)
```

And, of course, VSCode for the sweet, sweet RAM hoarding

```{python}
code_pkg = Installable(
    name="code-server",
    kind="binary",
    path="/usr/local/bin/code-server",
    commands=[
        """
        curl -Lk 'https://code.visualstudio.com/sha/download?build=stable&os=cli-alpine-x64'
        tar -xf vscode_cli.tar.gz

        test -x /usr/local/bin/code-server
        /usr/local/bin/code-server --version
        """
    ]
)
```

Validate the developer affordances.

```{python}
#| eval: false
show_spython(
    spython_exec(
        """
        echo "rv: $(which rv)"
        echo "arf: $(which arf)"
        echo "spack: $(which spack)"
        rv --version
        arf --version
        """,
        writable=True,
        bind_project=True,
    )
)
```
